excerpt.zh:
一颗本应“正常”的熔岩星球，让科研船的传感器出现了无法控制的故障。

建议进行进一步研究。
excerpt.en:
What should be a "normal" molten planet is making the Science Ship's sensors glitch uncontrollably.

Further study is advised.

Further study is advised.

texts.zh:
与在[From.Planet.GetName]表面上遇到的复杂情况相比，在轨科研船的传感器引发的骚动简直是小巫见大巫。来源不明的极端磁场波动甚至使设备失控。

研究这种电磁混乱将是一个相当严峻的考验——但只要有足够的时间，我们会得到答案的。
texts.en:
The disturbances caused by the orbiting Science Ship's sensors are nothing compared to the complications being encountered down on the surface of [From.Planet.GetName]. Extreme magnetic fluctuations from some unknown source are making equipment go haywire.

It will be quite an ordeal to research this electromagnetic bedlam - but given enough time, answers will emerge.

texts.zh:
就在地面考察队设法排除了失灵设备的故障后，剧烈波动的天然磁场终于揭开了它的神秘面纱。

[From.Planet.GetName]上汹涌的熔岩海洋与岩浆河流并非是普通的岩浆——那是熔融的金属！这种温度下的金属不会呈现出太强的磁性，[From.Planet.GetName]上的熔融金属更是不可能产生如此规模的电磁场。这究竟是怎么一回事？
texts.en:
Once the surface expedition managed to solve the problems with the malfunctioning equipment, the nature of the wild magnetic fluctuations started to reveal itself.

The raging oceans and rivers of lava down on [From.Planet.GetName] are in fact not made up of conventional magma - it's molten metal! Metals of this temperature tend not to have particularly strong magnetic properties; not even the sheer volume of molten metal on [From.Planet.GetName] should create electromagnetism on this scale. So what is causing it?

texts.zh:
[FromFrom.Planet.GetName]轨道上的这艘科学飞船终于解开了行星磁场波动之谜。

数百万年前，这颗行星靠近了一种特殊的中子星。这颗中子星的磁性或多或少地把[FromFrom.Planet.GetName]内部的金属熔化了。将它们变成我们今天看到的熔融海洋。目前所遇到的电磁现象，与诱发的大灾变的电磁现象相比，绝对是小巫见大巫。

那颗中子星现在在哪里仍然是个谜。一个相当令人不安的谜。
texts.en:
The Science Ship orbiting [FromFrom.Planet.GetName] has finally cracked the enigma of the magnetic fluctuations down on the planet.

Millions of years ago, the planet came into close proximity with a special kind of neutron star. The magnetism of this neutron star effectively boiled the metals inside [FromFrom.Planet.GetName], turning them into the molten oceans we see today. The electromagnetism we've encountered is but a lingering echo of the original, cataclysmic event.

Where the neutron star is now remains a mystery - a quite disturbing mystery.

texts.zh:
对传统物理定律的公然漠视使得科学部门认为“外力”可以解释[FromFrom.Planet.GetName]的奇怪特性。

撞击坑——以及轨道上的核聚变驱动粒子痕迹——表明这颗行星实际上在某个时刻被某种超级电子武器击中。这次严重的冲击使得行星上所有的金属都熔化了，而行星上仍然充斥着“残余电荷”。

究竟是什么导致了如此可怕的攻击，我们不得而知。
texts.en:
The blatant disregard for conventional laws of physics has our science department considering "external forces" as an explanation for the strange properties of [FromFrom.Planet.GetName].

An impact crater - in combination with fusion drive particle traces found in orbit - suggests that the planet was fired upon by some kind of electric super-weapon at some point. The severity of the strike was such that all metals on the planet melted, and the planet is still crackling with residual electricity.

What warranted such tremendous attack? We'll never know.

texts.zh:
传感器重新校准后，抵消了干扰的它立马有了新发现：一个邻近卫星上的废弃研究站。几近彻底烧毁的记录中抢救出的数据碎片详细描述了一个涉及星球表面巨型人造磁铁的实验。

实验有些过于成功了。它将整个行星的金属外壳变成了熔池，无比强烈的电磁电荷瞬间就炸毁了研究站。

嗯……没有牺牲就没有进展。
texts.en:
Once the sensors had been re-calibrated to compensate for the interference, a new discovery was made: an abandoned research station, located on a nearby moon. Fragments of data were salvaged from the almost entirely burned-out records, detailing an experiment involving a giant, artificial magnet on the planet's surface.

The experiment was a bit too successful. It turned the planet's entire, metal crust into molten pools with an electromagnetic charge so intense that it fried the research station in an instant.

Well... No progress without sacrifice.
